summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining Gaussian processes, principal component analysis, and uncertainty quantification to handle time-dependent transient responses. Specifically, functional principal component analysis reduces high-dimensional responses, enabling surrogate-based inverse uncertainty quantification as demonstrated in paper:2307.05592.

target_user.text: The target users are unverified, as the evidence bundle contains no patent assignee categories, though open-source repositories and packages such as repo:google/uncertainty-baselines and pkg:netcal indicate machine learning practitioners and researchers working on probabilistic modeling and calibration.

jtbd.text: Perform inverse uncertainty quantification for time-dependent transient experimental responses and physical model parameters while mitigating the high computational cost of direct inference.

value_prop.text: Reduces the dimensionality of complex transient simulation outputs using functional principal component analysis while preserving temporal profiles, thereby making downstream Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification efficient.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is designated as axis V (viability) due to missing evidence in the bundle, specifically whether commercial customers will pay for a software package combining functional principal components and Gaussian process surrogate models for transient uncertainty quantification.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test with a proposed threshold of 500 dollars per month for a pilot license, targeting industrial engineering teams to test viability and willingness to pay.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: A successful validation outcome is defined as a proposed threshold of at least 40 percent of interviewed organizations confirming budget availability and willingness to pay the pilot price.

kill_criteria.text: The opportunity should be killed if fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of interviewed prospective users express willingness to pay for the proposed software capability.

open_source.use: Used to provide baseline implementations of standard uncertainty quantification methods for evaluation.
Used for evaluating and calibrating probabilistic uncertainty estimates generated by the surrogate models.
Used to handle emulation and calibration for complex computer models with deep Gaussian processes.

to_build.text: Build a modular pipeline that integrates functional principal component analysis for time-series alignment and dimensionality reduction with Gaussian process surrogate training for inverse uncertainty quantification.
